dsa5101-orientation.title: Scalable-design decision map
dsa5101-orientation.learningGoal: Choose the first evidence to inspect when a data workflow must scale beyond one machine.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The course information establishes the scope; the textbook supplies a compact systems vocabulary for reasoning about scale.

nodes.label: Data passes
nodes.detail: How many full reads are required?

nodes.label: Working memory
nodes.detail: Can the state fit on one worker?

dsa5101-orientation.explanation: The map turns a vague scalability claim into four inspectable questions before implementation details distract you.

dsa5101-frequent-itemsets.title: Association-rule reasoning studio
dsa5101-frequent-itemsets.learningGoal: Separate counting baskets, pruning candidates, and interpreting a rule's conditional strength.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The lecture and assignment establish the calculation workflow; MMDS provides the full frequent-itemset chapter as labeled depth.

exercises.label: Support
exercises.prompt: How does a basket table become a support value?
exercises.takeaway: Count qualifying transactions first; normalize only after the numerator is explicit.
steps: Identify the baskets containing every item in the candidate.
Divide by the total number of transactions.
Use downward closure to remove every superset safely.
Only after frequent sets are known should rule confidence be interpreted.

exercises.label: Confidence
exercises.prompt: Why is the antecedent the denominator?
exercises.takeaway: Confidence is conditional: among baskets with A, how often does B also occur?
steps: Start with the baskets that already contain the antecedent.
The denominator is the antecedent support, not all baskets.
A high conditional rate can still add little information when B is common.

exercises.label: Interest
exercises.prompt: What does a base-rate comparison add?
exercises.takeaway: Lift or interest asks whether the consequent is more likely than its background frequency.
steps: Measure how common the consequent is without conditioning.
Measure how common B is among A baskets.
A value above one indicates positive association under this measure.
A rule can be predictive without proving that A causes B.

dsa5101-frequent-itemsets.explanation: Each tab isolates a different denominator or interpretation so support, confidence, and lift do not blur together.

dsa5101-minhash-lsh.title: MinHash-to-LSH trace
dsa5101-minhash-lsh.learningGoal: Follow the chain from set similarity to compact signatures and then to candidate generation.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The assignment requires the probability calculation; MMDS supplies the derivation and parameter trade-off as textbook depth.

steps: Define similarity before choosing a sketch.
A collision is an unbiased similarity signal under a random permutation.
At least one matching band is enough to pass the candidate filter.
LSH generates candidates; it does not certify every candidate as a true neighbor.
dsa5101-minhash-lsh.explanation: The trace keeps exact similarity, compact estimation, and approximate candidate retrieval as three different operations.

dsa5101-ranking-streams.title: Ranking and sketch selection lab
dsa5101-ranking-streams.learningGoal: Match a data question to PageRank, DGIM, or Flajolet–Martin without treating every stream method as interchangeable.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Assignment prompts define the current practice boundary; MMDS links the algorithms to their distinct outputs and error models.

splits.label: Rank nodes by link structure
splits.detail: Use stationary probability mass and damping.

splits.label: Count recent 1s in a window
splits.detail: Use timestamped buckets and bounded memory.

splits.label: Estimate distinct stream items
splits.detail: Use hash zero-prefix evidence and accept approximation.

dsa5101-ranking-streams.explanation: The right method follows the target quantity: node importance, a recent-window count, or distinct-cardinality estimation.
